QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_23

question.text: Under Regulation 27, the Manager/Sponsor must maintain records (valuation policies, investment rationale, investor particulars, etc.) for a minimum period of:

answer.text: 3 years after winding up of the fund
5 years after winding up of the fund
7 years from the date of record creation

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 27 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations requires record retention for 5 YEARS after the winding up of the fund. The 5-year clock starts POST wind-up, not from record-creation date. The Trap: 3 years understates. 7 years matches the Income Tax Act retention but not SEBI AIF. 10 years from final close is incorrect — period starts from wind-up. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C tests record-retention periods across SEBI regimes (Broker: 5; PM: 5; RA: 5). XIX-C focuses on the AIF-specific start date (post wind-up). Manager's Pro-Tip: Move records to immutable cloud storage with WORM (write-once-read-many) controls at wind-up — GP teams disperse fast after final distribution and physical archives get lost. SEBI inspection 4 years post wind-up is not uncommon.
